scope: Buffalo Color / Oldbury / Niagara Electro-Chemical-Roessler & Hasslacher-DuPont

findings.claim: Building 432 was built in 1917 and subsequently used for picric acid after the 1920s; its phosgene role is tentative in this investigation.
findings.locator: Printed 2-3, section 2.2.3; visually checked PDF page 5
findings.limit: Separate DEC 2015 history identifies Area D phosgene production; building-level uncertainty must not erase the area-level account.

findings.claim: Metal sludges were dewatered and shipped to recyclers; ash and chemical residues from burning were left in pits and soil covered.
findings.locator: Printed 2-4, section 2.2.5; visually checked PDF page 6
findings.limit: No attribution to a particular WWI-agent or picric-acid waste batch. Separate southwest concrete pit has uncertain function.

findings.claim: Oldbury began sodium perchlorate in 1908 and potassium perchlorate in 1910.
findings.locator: Appendix B: Joseph C. Schumacher 1999 paper, printed paper page 2 / PDF page 82
findings.limit: NASA hosts the paper; it did not author it. Early salt production does not prove later military-grade ammonium production dates or a waste destination.

findings.claim: Niagara Electro-Chemical sodium works was recently operating by December 1896; the contemporary account dates establishment to 1895.
findings.limit: Buffalo Avenue factory and Necco Park landfill are separate properties.

findings.claim: Manufacturing lineage includes Roessler & Hasslacher merger in 1925 and DuPont acquisition in 1930.
findings.locator: Reproduction of Hagley collection description; original link https://findingaids.hagley.org/repositories/3/resources/1200/collection_organization
findings.limit: Original archive blocked automated reading. Catalog reproduction is identified as such. Company-wide acquisition products must not all be assigned to Niagara.

findings.claim: Niagara Plant historical practices included bare-ground solvent washouts, cyanide-material weathering, PCB-oil drainage and reactor wastes directed toward Gill Creek.
findings.limit: Historical insurance opinion, not a current exposure assessment. Adjacent section I.A describes Pompton Lakes, New Jersey, and must not be imported into Niagara.

findings.claim: EPA identified specific sodium-process, chlorinated-manufacturing and solvent-bearing waste categories at Necco.
findings.limit: Mid-1930s-1977 disposal inventory does not establish destinations of all earlier company waste streams.

findings.claim: 2024 review found short-term protection with no current exposures, requiring emerging-contaminant delineation, source investigation and treatment-system sampling.
findings.locator: Printed 14-15 and 18; protectiveness table visually checked PDF page 19
findings.limit: PFAS and 1,4-dioxane occurred upgradient and downgradient. September 30, 2026 milestone is not evidence of completed follow-up; DEC public listing reviewed has no subsequent report.

openQuestions: Building 432 operating dates, picric-acid customers, and specific residue destinations.
Actual National Aniline mustard output, distinct from planned daily capacity.
Reconcile conflicting Niagara military-grade ammonium-perchlorate start dates and find plant waste records; do not assign pre-1956 Oldbury activity to Hooker ownership.
Obtain Necco emerging-contaminant follow-up to the September 2026 milestone and EPA disposition.
